content.text: Three consecutive green deploys (103, 104, 105). One cosmetic problem: a *successful* deploy still prints `error: interrupted by SIGTERM` because my trap kills the `just db-tunnel` child. Fixing so green means green.

input.old_string:
just db-tunnel &
    tunnel=$!
    trap 'kill $tunnel 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
input.new_string:
# stderr suppressed: tearing the tunnel down at EXIT makes the child `just` report SIGTERM,
    # which would otherwise print an error on a perfectly good deploy. The wait loop below is what
    # actually reports a tunnel that failed to come up.
    just db-tunnel 2>/dev/null &
    tunnel=$!
    trap 'kill $tunnel 2>/dev/null; wait $tunnel 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT

git add -A && git commit -q -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Verify the schema applied by checking collections exist

applySchema required a re-diff to come back empty. Directus 12.3.1
fills in collection metadata the committed snapshot doesn't carry
(meta.status, meta.autosave_revision_interval), so the diff is never
empty and every successful apply was reported as a failure. Verified
against the live instance: apply returns 204, all 11 collections are
created, and the re-diff still reports 11 pending - property-level
deltas only, no field or relation changes.

Check the owned collections exist afterward instead. That answers the
question the check was actually for and is immune to normalisation.

Also in this commit:
- just deploy takes pass-through args (`just deploy --yes`), needed to
  run it non-interactively at all.
- db-tunnel fails loudly when the VM/IP lookup comes back empty; a
  transient gcloud auth failure returns empty strings rather than a
  non-zero exit, which built a nonsense ssh command.
- The tunnel teardown no longer reports SIGTERM on a successful deploy.

Refs #112
EOF
)" && git push -q && git log --oneline -3
